title: Strict transform commutes with flat étale base change under generic-point control
statement: Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ be the blowup of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [def-nagata-global-blowup], let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $v:W\to X$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] (in particular, $v$ may be étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]). Assume that every irreducible component of $Z\times_XW$ has generic point mapping to the generic point of an irreducible component of $Z$ (equivalently, no component of the pullback lies over a proper closed subset of its corresponding component). Write $Z^{\mathrm{st}}\hookrightarrow X^+$ for the strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Then the canonical flat-base-change identification $X^+\times_XW\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_W}(W)$ [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], with $\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], identifies $Z^{\mathrm{st}}\times_XW$ with the strict transform of $Z\times_XW$ in $X^+\times_XW$; this equality is scheme-theoretic closure of the common inverse image of $Z\setminus V(\mathcal I)$.

source.place: Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image (flat base change of the quasi-compact scheme-theoretic image defining the strict-transform closure)

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, $W^+=X^+\times_XW$, $Z_W=Z\times_XW$, and $U_W=U\times_XW$. By [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] and [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], the comparison $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_W}(W)\to W\times_XX^+$ is an isomorphism over $W$; compose with the exchange of the two factors to identify its target with $W^+$. The complement of the extended ideal is $U_W$: locally if $\mathcal I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, both are $\bigcup_iD(a_i)$ after applying the ring map. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $X^+|_U\cong U$ and the corresponding base-changed restriction is $W^+|_{U_W}\cong U_W$. These are the restrictions of the same structure map, so the identification carries the preserved open to the preserved open.

Let $T=Z\times_XX^+$ and let $j:\Omega=T\times_XU\hookrightarrow T$ be its preserved open immersion. Under step 1, $\Omega\cong Z\times_XU$. Let $S\hookrightarrow T$ be its scheme-theoretic closure; by [def-nagata-strict-transform], $S=Z^{\mathrm{st}}$. The immersion $j$ is quasi-compact: on an affine neighborhood on which the pulled-back ideal has generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$, its source is the finite union $\bigcup_iD(a_i)$ of quasi-compact principal opens. This is a local check on the target, so no global quasi-compactness of $X$ or $Z$ is assumed. On $\Omega$ the ideal defining $S$ is zero, since a function there restricting to zero on $\Omega$ is zero. Thus $S\cap\Omega=\Omega$ scheme-theoretically, and the factor $h:\Omega\to S$ is an open immersion. The same finite-principal-open argument on $S$ makes $h$ quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated because its diagonal is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; the supported-section ideal is the kernel of restriction to the preserved open

proof.text: For $i:S\hookrightarrow T$, the kernel construction in [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] gives $i_*\mathcal O_S=\mathcal O_T/J$, where $J=\ker(\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_\Omega)$, since $j$ is quasi-compact. The induced map $i_*\mathcal O_S\to j_*\mathcal O_\Omega=i_*h_*\mathcal O_\Omega$ is injective: it is the map from a sheaf modulo the kernel of a sheaf homomorphism. Hence $\mathcal O_S\to h_*\mathcal O_\Omega$ is injective as well, by evaluating on opens of $S$, each an intersection with an open of $T$. The image kernel of $h$ is zero, so its scheme-theoretic image is all of $S$. This quotient-kernel argument retains nonreduced structure.

Set $S_W=S\times_XW$ and $T_W=T\times_XW$. The map $S_W\to S$ is the base change of the flat morphism $v:W\to X$, so it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to $h:\Omega\to S$ and $S_W\to S$: $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 2 and has scheme-theoretic image $S$ by step 3. It follows that $\Omega\times_SS_W=\Omega\times_XW$ has scheme-theoretic image $S_W$ in $S_W$. The same finite-principal-open check of step 2 on $S_W$ makes this open immersion quasi-compact. In particular, since this open immersion is quasi-compact, [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] identifies its image ideal with the kernel of restriction from $\mathcal O_{S_W}$ to this open, which is therefore zero.

Write $\Omega_W=\Omega\times_XW$. Associativity of fibre products and step 1 give $T_W=Z_W\times_WW^+$ and $\Omega_W=T_W\times_WU_W$. The closed subscheme $S_W\subset T_W$ contains this open. Its defining ideal is exactly the kernel of $\mathcal O_{T_W}\to (\Omega_W\hookrightarrow T_W)_*\mathcal O_{\Omega_W}$: the map factors through $\mathcal O_{S_W}$, and step 4 says that the second map has zero kernel. Thus $S_W$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of $\Omega_W$ in $T_W$, which is the strict transform of $Z_W$ by [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Finally $T_W\to W^+$ is a closed immersion: on affine opens it is the quotient by the extended ideal defining $Z\subset X$, using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Passing from closed subschemes of $T_W$ to closed subschemes of $W^+$ takes their quotient ideals to inverse-image ideals, and therefore preserves the equality just proved. This is the required equality inside $W^+=X^+\times_XW$, with its prescribed inclusions. The proof applies to the assumed generic-point situation; no use of that extra hypothesis is necessary. An étale $v$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so that case is included.
